observations.metric: WXS mutation enrichment: significant_q05 = 1 of 22 tested; min q = 0.00031
observations.finding: BAP1 is significantly enriched (set 36.7% vs rest 2.7%; OR=20.6, 95% CI 4.19–100.7; Fisher p=1.4e-05; q=0.00031). PBRM1 is depleted (set 20.0% vs rest 45.2%; OR=0.30, 95% CI 0.11–0.83; q=0.27).

observations.metric: CNV characterization: continuous significant_q05 = 0 of 49; gain/loss significant_q05 = 0 of 107; min q = 0.869
observations.finding: No CNV feature reaches q<0.05. The largest continuous effect is chr14q (Cliff's delta=-0.32, lower in set) and the largest gain/loss difference is chr14q::loss (56.7% vs 34.2%; OR=2.51, 95% CI 1.05–5.99), but all q-values are 0.869.

biological_support.statistical_interpretation: RNA shows a coherent immune/inflammatory up-regulation pattern (allograft rejection, interferon alpha/gamma, IL6-JAK-STAT3) with moderate-to-large SMDs and FDR-controlled significance. CNV shows no FDR-significant differences; the nominal chr14q loss enrichment is exploratory only. Availability is complete for RNA (30 vs 73), WXS (30 vs 73), and CNV (30 vs 73).
biological_support.medical_interpretation: The RNA and WXS findings are consistent with a biologically distinct subset characterized by immune pathway activation and BAP1 mutation enrichment, but the CNV evidence is weak and does not independently support this pattern. These are molecular associations, not prognostic or mechanistic claims.
limitations: CNV effects are not FDR-significant and should be treated as exploratory.
The BAP1 odds ratio CI is wide.
